findings.first_pass_finding: Theorem A1 (the rank envelope R_opt with its sharpness proof) is a concrete advance (N1) and not new ground (N2): it is the joint optimisation over scale and weight of a known trace bound (Lemma 3.2 of Alpoge and Furman, arXiv:2608.13637v2, whose Remark 3.3 already optimises the coefficient at Q = 0), plus a compression to the complement of the positive eigenspace of Q, plus a sharpness proof.
findings.reason: Symbol-by-symbol correspondence. (1) Knausgard Lemma 6.1 says: for t >= c, tr A^2 >= tr phi_c(P) + 2t(tr A - tr P) - t^2 p. Take c = 1 and use phi_1(x) >= 2x - 1 for x > 0. This gives r >= 2u + 2Ct - C^2 b - S for every C >= 1 (Knausgard's t is the team's C, his p is the team's b). That is exactly the family of A1 part 1 and docs/10, and the team's own THEOREMS.md section 0.3 says so. (2) Alpoge-Furman Lemma 3.2 is the member C = 2. (3) Remark 3.3 ('setting Q = 0 and optimising the coefficient 2 recovers rank P >= (tr P)^2/||P||^2') is the rescaling P -> sP at Q = 0, i.e. R_opt at t = 0, b = 0. (4) The team's additions are three. (i) The target n+(H_perp) in place of rank P: a one-line Cauchy-interlacing substitution into the same proof. (ii) The joint supremum over s > 0 and C >= 1: C* = st/b, so regime 1 holds exactly when t(u+t) >= bS, which is two-variable calculus. (iii) The pointwise integer sharpness min rank P = max(1, ceil R_opt). None of the three papers has (iii): Lemma 3.2 gives only its equality case, and section 7.2(b) gives sharpness for one zeta configuration. (iii) is the strongest piece and survives the prior-art search. But it is an elementary explicit construction. THEOREMS.md states it without a written proof: the team's evidence is the float case-split constructor in check_003 (which contains a 1e12-for-1e-12 typo in one guard), and exact witnesses exist only from the evaluator. Under PROTOCOL.md, closing the open question of the best bound from (tr P, tr Q, ||H||^2, b) is 'a newly closed/tightened bound', which is N1. It is not a new invariant or a cross-domain map. The evaluator's N1 is right. Its phrase 'small clean steps on known parts' undersells (iii), which is not a known part.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: For P >= 0 and n+(Q) <= b, R_opt(u,t,S,b) (the closed-form joint supremum over scale and weight C >= 1 of the known Knausgard/docs-10 family, of which Alpoge-Furman Lemma 3.2 is the C = 2 member) lower-bounds n+(Pi_{W-perp} H Pi_{W-perp}), and hence rank P. It is exactly sharp as a function of (u,t,S,b): for every realisable tuple with u > 0 the minimum rank of P is max(1, ceil R_opt). No bound using only these four numbers can certify more. Label N1 (upper end), with the sharpness theorem as the new part. It would need a written proof in THEOREMS.md before any stronger label is argued.

findings.first_pass_finding: Theorem A2 (the Stieltjes-Hankel moment hierarchy) is the classical one-sided Chebyshev-Markov-Stieltjes moment method (sharp version: a Christoffel function), which section 7.2(d) of the same paper already names. So it is known (the team labels AUDIT-014 as N2).
findings.reason: The mechanism of A2 is classical. tr f(H) <= n+(H) for a polynomial f <= indicator(lambda > 0), with f = 1 - q^2, is the polynomial-minorant (Markov-Krein / Chebyshev-Markov-Stieltjes) method. The cited paper names it in 7.2(d), and the extra step n+(H) <= b + n+(H_perp) is Cauchy interlacing. As a theorem A2 is N0, and N2 does not survive. Two corrections to the evaluator's wording follow from my own runs. (1) 'Sharp version: a Christoffel function' is false for n+. 1 - Lambda_m(0) bounds the nonzero-eigenvalue fraction, not the positive one. Exact counterexamples: G = -I_3 gives 1 - Lambda_1(0) = 1 with n+ = 0; diag(1,-1) gives 1 - Lambda_2(0) = 1 with n+/d = 1/2. The team's constraint (nonnegative alternating coefficients, so q >= 1 on (-inf,0]) is the correct one-sided restriction, and for m = 2 it is exactly the set of admissible single squares. So the team's statement is more correct than the literal remark it would be reduced to. (2) A2 is not the sharp one-sided bound either. On 200 random mixed-sign spectra the sharp degree-4 LP exceeds R_H4 by more than 0.1 in 174 cases and certifies a larger integer in 167 (it never exceeded n+). On PSD H, including both team examples, the two coincide. So A2 is a restricted, explicitly solvable case of the classical method, not the classical sharp bound and not new.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: A2 is a correct instance of the classical one-sided moment method applied to H = P + Q and combined with interlacing. It uses the correct one-sided sign constraint, which the cited informal remark omits, and it has an exact closed form for m = 2 (R_H4) and an exact KKT solution for m = 3. Exact rank recovery for PSD H with at most m distinct eigenvalues is a classical Gauss-quadrature fact. On the project instance Scan 23848 Mode B it lifts the certificate to exactly 1 for every rho, where R_opt and c = 2 fail. Label: N0 as a theorem, N1 for the closed form and its application to that instance.

findings.first_pass_finding: The claim that A4 "strictly beats both" R_opt and the degree-4 A2 bound holds only on hand-picked matrices: on 1,600 fresh exact matrices A4 never certified a larger integer rank than A2 did, and in the team's own benchmark the degree-6 A2 bound equals A4.
findings.reason: Team examples, exactly. Diagonal case: R_opt = 24/17, R_H4 - 1 = 1.4498, A4 = 3 = n+(H_perp), R_H6 - 1 = 3. Non-commuting eps = 1/200 case: R_opt = 1.6821, R_H4 - 1 = 1.8866, A4 >= 2.5931 with my optimum (the team's quoted 2.3737 is a valid lower value), R_H6 - 1 = 3.0000 (just below 3), n+(H_perp) = 3. So the team's literal claim is true: there exist non-commuting complex matrices where A4 certifies 3 while ceil R_opt = ceil(R_H4 - b) = 2. The evaluator's 'only on hand-picked matrices' is too strong. On a structured family (one large isolated Q+ eigenvalue, P weakly coupled by a small complex Cayley rotation), A4 beats both in integer terms in 29/300, 19/300 and 24/300 fresh samples. In those 24 cases A4 also beats the sharp classical degree-4 bound that uses only S1..S4 and b, so its gain comes from new information (tr Q through Weyl (W2)), not from A2's single-square restriction. The evaluator is right on generality and on degree 6. A fully optimised A4 never beat R_H4 - b on generic or regime-1 random matrices: 0/1,200 over two seeds, even though room was left in 163 to 173 of 300 generic cases. R_H6 - b certified at least as much as A4 in all 1,800 cases, and strictly more in up to 139/300. The evaluator's own '1,600' evidence used only 4 random A4 parameter draws plus the team's finder, and it was inferred from equal 'beats ceil R_opt' counts. My full optimisation supports its conclusion on generic inputs.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: A4 is a valid exact bound. On a structured, non-generic class of complex non-commuting matrices (one large isolated positive eigenvalue of Q, P weakly coupled) it certifies a strictly larger integer than ceil R_opt, ceil(R_H4 - b) and every bound built only from S1..S4 and b (about 6 to 10 percent of fresh samples in that class). It did so in 0 of 1,200 generic random samples, and it never exceeded R_H6 - b, which uses S5 and S6. Label N1.

findings.first_pass_finding: The first identity (the squared residual after absorbing a failed anchor rises by exactly e1^2/|p1|^2) is the textbook restricted least squares formula RSS_r = RSS_ur + (R b - r)'[R (X'X)^-1 R']^-1 (R b - r), so it is known mathematics (the team labels it N1, a concrete advance).
findings.reason: The two routes match symbol by symbol. X = Phi, Y = y, q = 1 restriction R = a1^T Phi, r = a1^T y, and Rb = r says the same as a1.(y - Phi b) = 0, which is the anchor being silenced. Then R beta_hat - r = -e1 and R(X'X)^-1R' = a1^T P a1 = |p1|^2. The restricted residual e~ = e_hat + X(X'X)^-1R'[.]^-1(R beta_hat - r) equals r* - (e1/|p1|^2) p1, which is exactly r_adapt. RSS_r = RSS_ur + e1^2/|p1|^2. The RLS requirement that R have full row rank is the team's hypothesis p1 != 0. 'Minimum output-space shift' is the same object as the restricted fit, because |r* - Delta|^2 = |r*|^2 + |Delta|^2 for Delta in col(Phi). 'Any other silencing shift costs more' is RLS optimality. The team's code and report never cite restricted least squares, and PROTOCOL makes N0 mandatory for textbook results and requires the citation. The identity adds nothing to the textbook formula.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: Identity 1 is restricted least squares with one restriction (N0, cite RLS, e.g. Greene, Econometric Analysis, restricted least squares section). The N1 tag can be moved to the application, which docs/09 lacks: docs/09 6.2 says 'The demonstration does not show that adaptation harms outside anchors.' Under PROTOCOL's 'newly certified theorem on an untested case', the team's package certifies the following for the latch model of docs/09 6.1. Absorbing a failed anchor costs exactly e1^2/|p1|^2 in total squared residual. It raises the mean squared reading over isotropic fresh anchors by sigma^2 e1^2/|p1|^2. It helps a given fresh anchor exactly when 0 < x < 2. Each of these is a one-line corollary of RLS. Label: N1 for the application to our open Claim 9, N0 for the identity.

findings.first_pass_finding: The result does not "settle our Claim 9" or "decide Falsifier 6" as the team says. It gives an exact first half and reduces Falsifier 6 to a measurable condition. The half about revising the specification is not shown, and a wrong revision can raise the error against the truth. Our Claim 9 and Falsifier 6 are in siliconcordat/loom draft pull request 9, docs/09-gate-contracts.md.
findings.reason: The evaluator undersold one point. The team does state the second half and gets it right in its noiseless scope: ||r_rev||^2 = ||r*||^2 - ||P_rev_perp r*||^2 <= ||r*||^2 < ||r_adapt||^2, and a revision whose span contains r* zeros every anchor. So 'not shown' is too strong for the total residual in the noiseless model. The step is still the elementary fact that adding regressors cannot raise the residual. It does not show that revision 'then helps' in the sense Claim 9 needs. (a) Per anchor, even without noise, the team's own partial revision hurts the fresh anchor u2 - u3, moving it from 25 to 784/25. (b) With noise, a wrong added direction lowers the in-sample residual (20699/3600 -> 9337/1800) and raises the error against the truth (289/72 -> 659/144). The team's theorem says nothing about noise. (c) Falsifier 6 is an observation about real loops. A model theorem cannot decide it. It can only turn it into a measurable condition, the per-anchor x or the evaluator's ensemble sign. (d) The team's own identities count against 'settles Claim 9 via Falsifier 6': in the model, Falsifier 6 fires on same-kind anchors even though absorption closed none of the gap. See missed_by_the_evaluator.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: In the noiseless linear model of docs/09 6.1: (i) absorption costs exactly e1^2/|p1|^2 (RLS) and leaves the outside part (I-P)r = r* exactly unchanged; (ii) on a fresh anchor, a2.r_adapt = e2(1 - x), which helps iff 0 < x < 2; (iii) adding any direction weakly lowers the total residual, strictly iff it overlaps r*, and a revision containing r* zeros every anchor. This is an exact model of Claim 9's first half plus the total-residual form of its second half. Falsifier 6 is reduced to a measurable condition, not decided, and the noisy or per-anchor form of 'revision helps' stays open. findings.first_pass_finding: The "trace-slack law" Delta t* = w^2/q is a first-order estimate, not an exact law: in the team's own example the exact crossing is T tau* = 7/8 - 9 sqrt(15)/40 (about 0.00358) against the law's 1/360 (about 0.00278).
findings.reason: The evaluator is right that the law is not exact. I reproduce T tau* = 7/8 - 9 sqrt(15)/40 ~ 0.003579 for N = 0, and other noise gives other crossings: N = tau/2 I, the team's own noise level, gives 5/8 - sqrt(5565)/120 ~ 0.003342. The team's '~' derivation drops the 2w term and the Delta^2 terms, and the AUDIT row calls it exact. The steelman is that the law is a uniform sufficient condition, which neither side stated. Let E0 = D - tau I and F(N) = (m - t)^2 - (S - t^2). Since (tr N)^2 >= ||N||^2 for PSD N, F(N) >= F(0) + tr((4wI - 2E0)N) >= F(0) - 2 tau (q - 2w - tau). Equality holds at N = tau v v^T, noise aligned with the known component. So that is the exact worst case, with T tau*_worst = (43 - sqrt(1838))/44 ~ 0.0029113, only 4.8% above 1/360. The adversarial search agrees: its minimum is 6.9% above, never below. Exact R at T tau = 1/360 in the worst case is 32761/32019 > 1. At the law, F = 2w^3(20q + 11w)/(25q^2) > 0 for n = 5, and similar positive forms hold for n = 3 to 20 wherever the branch-1 condition holds, which it does in the team's example. So the evaluator's '13 to 29 percent higher' covers only three commuting families and overstates the slack in the worst case.

findings.first_pass_finding: The "Iterative Multi-Quotient Farkas Peeling Tower" is saturated cost partitioning from the planning literature (Seipp, Keller and Helmert, JAIR 2020): with each concrete transition as its own label, the saturated cost of a step u->v is h(pi u) - h(pi v) and their remaining-cost function (Definition 13) is the tower's reduced cost c^(j). So it is known (the team labels it N2, new ground).
findings.reason: The match is exact. Keller et al. 2016, Definition 4 (saturated state-dependent cost partitioning) defines c_1(a,s)=c(a); hat c_i(a,s)=h_i(alpha_i(s)) - h_i(alpha_i(s[a])), where h_i is the goal distance of T^{alpha_i} under c_i; and c_{i+1}=c_i - hat c_i. Each piece maps one to one. A deterministic (a,s) is a concrete step u->v. alpha_i is pi_j. The abstract transition weight is the minimum over the concrete transitions it stands for, which is the team's min_w. h_i is h_j*, the quotient LP optimum, which for a shortest-path LP is the goal distance. So c_{i+1}(u,v) = c^(j-1)(u,v) + h_j(pi_j v) - h_j(pi_j u), which is the tower's c^(j). The bound h^{scpD}(s) = sum_i h_i(alpha_i(s)) is the tower's H^(K). The 2020 JAIR paper gives the same result when every concrete transition is its own label. Eq. (1) then has a single abstract transition per label, so mscf(l) = h(pi u) - h(pi v). remain_i in Def. 13 is then c^(j). Order dependence is in the JAIR abstract, along with taking the max over several orders. Keller et al. Theorem 3 already shows that the transition-level variant and the operator-level variant are incomparable. This source is older and closer than the evaluator's citation, and it covers the team's exact variant. Things the team adds: an exact rational Farkas certificate at each layer, which is shortest-path LP duality (N0), and the residual identity d* - H = d*_res. That identity is Johnson reweighting. findings.first_pass_finding: The "Maslov-Doob" identity K_q(c + dH) = D^-1 K_q(c) D is a diagonal similarity and not a Doob transform: the result is not stochastic.
findings.reason: In the ordinary (+,x) semiring the evaluator is right. The identity is a diagonal similarity (gauge transform). 0 of 31 non-goal rows sum to 1 at every q, even when H = d*, because q^H is not harmonic for K_q. Calling it 'identically the Doob h-transform' at finite q is a misnomer. The steelman: under Maslov dequantization (q = e^{-beta}, with + replaced by max), the identity row max = q^{delta_trop(u)} holds exactly at every q tested, for both potentials. So D^-1 K_q D is max-times stochastic on every non-goal row (all 31 rows have max 1) exactly when delta_trop = 0 everywhere, which by F5 means H = d*. The 2-layer H has 3 states with delta > 0, and exactly 28 of 31 rows have max 1. Read this way, 'Maslov-Doob' is accurate: it is the max-times analogue of Doob's transform by the tropical harmonic function d*, which is the shortest-path potential. This diagonal rescaling is standard in max algebra (it resembles what is called 'visualization scaling'; I did not read a full-text source for that term, so I do not rely on it) and is in any case Johnson reweighting in multiplicative form. Label N0.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: For any potential H and every q in (0,1), K_q(c + dH) = D^-1 K_q(c) D with D = diag(q^H), and the row maxima of that matrix are exactly q^{delta_trop(u)}. So it is a max-times (tropical) Doob transform, row-stochastic in the max-times sense on every non-goal state, if and only if H = d*. In the ordinary semiring it is only a diagonal similarity. Label N0.

findings.first_pass_finding: The "Cohomological Optimality Theorem" is the standard Bellman or complementary-slackness condition for shortest paths.
findings.reason: 0 failures. The theorem is Bellman's equation together with its uniqueness. delta_trop(s) = min_v (c(s,v) + H(v)) - H(s) = 0 is exactly H(s) = min_v {c(s,v) + H(v)}, which is Bertsekas (3.11a) with the arcs reversed: node 1 becomes the goal (several goals become one contracted sink), d_j becomes H(s), and a_ij becomes c(s,v). H(goal) = 0 is (3.11b). Co-reachability is his 'path from 1 to every node', under which d* satisfies (3.11). The team's c > 0 gives his 'all cycles have positive length', under which Exercise 3.12 says d* is the only solution, and he notes it fails with a zero-length cycle. The team's argument that 'd^0 integrates to 0 on cycles' is the standard fact that a cycle's reduced cost equals its cost. The only differences are the reduced-cost and coboundary notation and the name 'commutation defect' for delta_trop. Label N0.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: For costs c > 0 and every state co-reachable to the goal, a potential H with H(goal) = 0 equals d* if and only if its tropical defect delta_trop(s) = min_v c_red(s,v) is 0 at every non-goal state. This is Bellman's equation and its uniqueness (Bertsekas 1991, Eq. 3.11 and Ex. 3.12). Exact and correct, with a useful per-state diagnostic of where a bound is not tight. Label N0.

findings.first_pass_finding: Theorem A (a chain of scales with error boxes admits values with every step slope inside a rational bracket if and only if an integer inequality holds for every pair i < j) is consistency of a simple temporal problem on a chain (Dechter, Meiri and Pearl 1991) written in integer form. So it is known (the team labels it N1).
findings.reason: Exact correspondence. DMP node X_0 is the origin. X_i is h_i = ln y~_i. The box is two edges, 0->i with weight ln U_i and i->0 with weight -ln L_i. The step bracket is two edges, i->i+1 with weight alpha+ ln(x_{i+1}/x_i) and i+1->i with weight -alpha- ln(x_{i+1}/x_i). In a graph made of a chain plus a hub, the only simple cycles are two trivial 2-cycles (L_i<=U_i and alpha-<=alpha+) and two kinds of hub cycle. The cycle 0->j->...->i->0 has weight ln U_j - ln L_i - alpha- ln(x_j/x_i). The cycle 0->i->...->j->0 has weight ln U_i + alpha+ ln(x_j/x_i) - ln L_j. By Theorem 3.1 the system is feasible iff these weights are >= 0. Exponentiating and raising to q1, q2 > 0 gives exactly the team's (U_j/L_i)^q1 >= (x_j/x_i)^p1 and (L_j/U_i)^q2 <= (x_j/x_i)^p2. The only difference from DMP is the log-free cross-multiplied integer encoding, which follows from exp being monotone and the exponents rational. The local-yes/global-no gap is the classical gap between checking constraints locally and checking the whole network. I looked for a reading under which the team's N1 survives. The N1 label also covers 'live falsification', but K41 failing on this same Sabra model is already certified in the repo README at over 80 and 50 standard errors, and rising D_eff is already reported there. The remaining N1 route is 'newly discovered concrete defect with minimal reproducer' against draft #58's sentence that steps and all pairs always agree. The team's own note says #58 explicitly excluded error bars, so this is a scope extension, not a defect. The theorem is correct but known.

This holds on live Sabra F2/F6 at +-5 SE (team seeds 1 and 7; evaluator 16 of 16 fresh seeds). It is the log-free integer form of STP consistency on a chain (DMP 1991 Thm 3.1). findings.first_pass_finding: Theorem B (four rays are complete for log-convexity or log-concavity of four dyadic points inside error boxes) is the discrete case of the convexity sandwich theorem (Baron, Matkowski and Nikodem 1994): a convex function fits between L and U if and only if every three-point chord of U dominates L. For m points the complete set is the C(m,3) chord triples. So it is known (the team labels it N2).
findings.reason: Correspondence: D=[0,m-1], k=log2(x_k/x_0), f=ln L and g=ln U at the grid points. BMN is stated for functions on a convex domain, and the team's data live on 4 points. The finite version therefore needs one short step: pad f with -M and g with +M off the grid, or take the greatest convex minorant of the U points directly (the envelope argument BMN use for sufficiency). The chord conditions are then (k-i) ln L_j <= (k-j) ln U_i + (j-i) ln U_k for i<j<k. For m=4 equally spaced points these are exactly the team's four rays, exponentiated. So 'discrete case of BMN' is accurate as a direct corollary, not as BMN's literal statement; that is a wording precision only. The team's own scope note (m=4 only; the m=5 separator '(3,2,1)' is the chord (0,1,4)) confirms the general answer is the chord triples. Under PROTOCOL.md, N2 requires a new theorem that survives prior-art search. No such search is recorded, and the result is a specialisation of a classical one. findings.first_pass_finding: Theorem 2's part on E_6 and E_7 is elementary and known (an index argument: det(D_n)/det(Gamma) is not a perfect square), and the label "uniqueness theorem" is misleading because the theorem says nothing about uniqueness of the H_8 curve.
findings.reason: The E6/E7 part is correct, elementary and known. It is a one-line index argument. It is also immediate from classical facts: D6 is not a full-rank root subsystem of E6, nor D7 of E7 (Borel-de Siebenthal), and the Delaunay cells of E6 and E7 are simplices, 2_21 and 3_21, never cross-polytopes. The D_n^+ part is also an elementary norm count. On the label I partly side with the team. The theorem states its uniqueness claim exactly: 'a bar-preserving fold F_n -> D_n^+ exists if and only if n = 8'. That is uniqueness of the dimension within the D_n^+ family, which is accurate, and nothing in the team's text claims uniqueness of the H8 curve. So 'misleading' narrows to 'ambiguous': the label invites a reader to think of curve uniqueness. Also, the 'only if' direction uses only the endpoint, and the 'if' direction is Theorem 1. What does stand is the novelty part: AUDIT-017's 'exact E6/E7/D_n^+ uniqueness theorem absent from prior art', counted inside the N2, is not supported.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: N0 (correct scope statement, elementary): no periodic packing of the form P_n + Lambda = Gamma + v0 can produce E6 or E7 at minimum norm 2, because det(D_n)/det(Gamma) would have to be a square. Within the family D_n^+ (n even), a bar-preserving cross-polytope endpoint exists only for n = 8, where D_8^+ = E8 is reached by Theorem 1. Better wording: 'dimension obstruction (n = 8 is the only D_n^+ target)', not 'uniqueness theorem'.

findings.first_pass_finding: "Computer-free" applies only to the all-n non-overlap proof. The non-overlap of the nilpotent C_4 fold rests on a finite certificate.
findings.reason: The evaluator's sentence is factually right, but no team sentence says otherwise. The team scoped 'computer-free' to the C_n family and to the E8 endpoint lemma, both of which are hand proofs. It stated plainly that C_4^nilp rests on a finite exact certificate. The only possible issue is that a reader skimming README or AUDIT-009 might bundle the items, and one clause would fix that. findings.strongest_surviving_claim: As written by the team: the F_n -> D_n non-overlap proof for every n >= 3 (twisted cycle C_n) is computer-free, using the discrete path Sobolev inequality and five degree-4 Bernstein coefficients in Z[sqrt2]. The C_4^nilp non-overlap is proved by an infinite-image bound plus an exact finite certificate (21,944 pairs). Label N1 for C_4^nilp. Optional one-clause clarification in README and AUDIT-009.

areas.recovered_by_the_second_pass:
1. The full text the evaluator could not get is openly available. The Wayback Machine copy of Smith ScholarWorks viewcontent.cgi?article=1262&context=csc_facpubs is the publisher PDF of Borcea and Streinu 2021, and section 7 does not anticipate the result (details under F1). With it read, the main reason for low confidence on the E8 label is gone. Nobody had noted the one related device: their twisted Hamiltonian cycle on the cross-polytope axes against the team's twisted cycle C_n. The team should cite it as related.
2. The parent repo's own v3 preprint (papers/source/main.tex line 379) lists 'analogous motions in dimensions n >= 4' as an open problem. PR 106 closes it for D_n (all n) and for E8. That is direct in-house evidence that the work is new, not repackaged.
3. The census discrepancy the evaluator left unchecked (864 in the proof against 2016 in check_006) is resolved. Both are correct, under different filters. Of the 20,736 Type-I 4x4 matrices, 2016 have det(2I+C) = 16, and 864 of those also put the 8 motif points in distinct cosets, so they are genuine D_4 endpoints. Among the 864, 48 are nilpotent (C^2 = 0) and 96 have I+S PSD. All of these numbers were reproduced with my own code (exact PSD test by principal minors).
4. A refinement nobody noted: the generic twisted C_4 is itself nilpotent (charpoly lambda^4, C^3 = 0, C^2 != 0), which matches the team's remark that D_4(d,t) = d^4. So 'a nilpotent fold exists only in n = 4' already holds for the C_n family. What is special about C_4^nilp is C^2 = 0 and the anticommuting symmetric and skew parts, a narrower point than the README suggests.
5. Lemma 5's Bernstein control points P0 = w0, P1 = w1 + sqrt2 m, P2 = 2 w1 do not depend on C. Hence any L = dI + tC fold with zero diagonal and unit rows reduces non-overlap to three integer inequalities. For C_4^nilp these held on all 216,512 pairs in [-4,4]^4, so a hand proof of the nilpotent fold looks within reach. This is a reusable template for other C, and it is the structural core of the D_n result.
6. Independent exact replication with no shared code (recheck_folds.py, run twice with byte-identical output) confirms the following. For n = 3..12: bars stay identically at sqrt2 and det L_n(1) = 4n. The motif points lie in distinct cosets, and the closed-form Chebyshev determinant holds for n = 3..9. Kissing number is 2n(n-1) for n = 3..8. Lemma 4/5 inequalities and Bernstein signs showed 0 violations on 245,122 box pairs and 5,999 random pairs with n up to 30 and entries up to 40. For E8 the replication covers the endpoint and lattice structure, a second shell enumeration done a different way (filtering E8 shells 2160 and 17520 down to 240 and 2160 vectors of Lambda), and a numeric sweep consistent with Loewner monotonicity and strict interior separation.
7. Undersold phenomenon: in every D_n and in E8, the motion is strictly overlap-free with only bars touching for s < 1. All endpoint contacts then appear at once at s = 1, with density strictly increasing throughout. The E8 proof's 2x2 block reduction with Loewner monotonicity G(s) >= G(1) is a neat, reusable device: it reduces the infinite non-overlap question to two finite shells, uniformly in s.

findings.first_pass_finding: "Unjamming" of the Barnes-Wall and Leech lattices is a much weaker property than the word suggests: the certified motion strictly increases volume, so it is consistent with those lattices being perfect and eutactic (locally optimal) and says nothing about local optimality. Without bars such a motion is trivial for any packing. The fair claim is a short overlap-free, bar-preserving fold of the cross-polytope framework with each lattice as an endpoint. Label N1, not N2.
findings.reason: The core of F1 holds. In the standard sense, lattice jamming means perfect plus eutactic, and BW16 and Leech are both. The team's arc strictly increases volume and leaves the lattice class: the motif stays rigid and only the sublattice deforms. So it neither contradicts jamming nor says anything about it, and in no standard sense (Torquato-Stillinger local, collective or strict) is it an unjamming. Two parts of F1 need narrowing. (a) 'Without bars such a motion is trivial for any packing' is too broad. For a general packing with a rigid motif, dilating the lattice need not be overlap-free. For this framework it is trivial, and the team proves exactly that in its own Lemma A, so the team already says the content lies in the bars. (b) 'Says nothing about local optimality' is true, but the team never claims otherwise. What fails is the word 'unjamming' or 'strictly unjammed', which collides with the established term. On the team's own definitions, N1 explicitly covers a 'newly certified theorem/obstruction on an untested case'. The realizations and arcs are exactly that: the F_n -> Gamma question, already settled for D_n and E_8, is now answered at n = 16 and 24. Nothing here is a sharp new invariant or a cross-domain map, so N2 does not hold.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: Label N1, exact. For n = 16 and n = 24 there are explicit rational bar matrices L = 2I + C with every row of C a minimal vector, such that P_n + Z^n L equals Lambda_16 + e_0 (index 32, det L = 2) and Leech/sqrt2 + e_0 (index 48, det L = 3/256). From each endpoint there is an explicit rational Cayley arc, of length tau in [0, 1/4000] for BW16 and [0, 1e-10] for Leech. Along it the motif stays rigid, all n bars stay at exactly sqrt 2, every other inter-cell contact strictly opens, the packing is overlap-free against all of Z^n, and the covolume strictly increases. Read backwards, each lattice is the endpoint of a short bar-preserving, overlap-free fold whose density rises into it. So the bar-constrained endpoint is not locked: it is not tensegrity-rigid. That is a necessary condition for any global fold F_n -> Lambda, and the arc proves it. Suggested wording: 'bar-preserving release arc' instead of 'unjamming'.

findings.first_pass_finding: "All lattice points strictly separate" is false as phrased: the contacts inside the motif (960 and 2,208 directed) and the 2n bar contacts stay at exactly sqrt 2. Only the other inter-cell contacts separate.
findings.reason: The quoted false statement is not in the team's text. Each detailed statement the team makes is correct and already states what F2 says. Lemma B lists bar pairs as staying at exactly sqrt 2 and covers the other inter-cell pairs separately. Theorems 2 and 3 report '32 exact bar zeros' and '48 exact bar zeros' and count only inter-cell contacts (32x4320 - 32x30, 48x196560 - 48x46), so motif contacts are left out by construction. What survives is a wording point about two summary phrases, the table's 'Strictly unjammed' and sec. 6's 'strict ... unjamming over all 137,280 / 9,432,672 contacts'. Read alone, they could suggest every contact opens, when 2n of those contacts are zero-velocity bars. As an accusation of a false claim, F2 falls. As a wording note, it stands.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: Exact, and the team already states it. On the certified arcs the motif contacts (960 and 2,208 directed) and the 2n bar contacts stay at exactly sqrt 2, and every other inter-cell contact opens strictly: first-order velocity at least delta (>1/7 for BW16, >=2/25 for Leech), and squared distance above 2 at every tau in (0, tau*]. The only fix needed is to the summary phrases: 'all non-bar inter-cell contacts strictly open'.

findings.first_pass_finding: In section 3 of the proof the step "positive symmetric part implies det L(tau) > det L" does not follow. The repair is that gate (1) already gives sigma_min(I + A) >= 1 + lambda_0 tau / 2 > 1, hence det(I + A) > 1.
findings.reason: The sentence as written does not follow, so the finding is right about the text. But the gap is one word wide, and the needed fact is already proved in the bullet just before it. That bullet shows y^T (I+A) y >= 1 + lam0 tau/2 for every unit y, so A_sym >= (lam0 tau/2) I > 0 and sigma_min(I+A) >= 1 + lam0 tau/2. Either repair closes the step. The evaluator's: |det| >= sigma_min^n > 1, with the sign fixed because (I+A)_sym > 0. Or an eigenvalue route: A_sym > 0 puts every eigenvalue of A in Re > 0, so every factor |1 + lambda| > 1 and det(I+A) > 1. Read with 'symmetric part of A' in place of 'of I + A', the team's sentence is valid. The derivative claim tr X >= n lam0 is correct. No result changes.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: Exact, and part of the N1 arc result above. On (0, tau*], A(tau)_sym >= (lam0 tau/2) I and sigma_min(I + A(tau)) >= 1 + lam0 tau/2. Hence det L(tau) = det L * det(I + A(tau)) > det L (strict volume expansion), with d/dtau ln det L(tau) at 0 equal to tr X >= n lam0. Fix: replace 'I_n + A(tau) has strictly positive symmetric part' with 'A(tau) has symmetric part >= (lam0 tau/2) I (previous bullet)'.

Sec. 5 names it ('exact rational projection of X0_24_INT_256/256'), the 24x24 integer table is in the verifier, and must-fail control C5 tests it. findings.first_pass_finding: AUDIT-019's stiffness object is the standard relaxed Cauchy-Born elasticity tensor of a central-force network, its rank-1 state is the known pentamode class (Milton and Cherkaev, Norris 2014), and the "master rank-1 stress formula" follows in two lines from torque balance (diag(tau) B symmetric) and the virial theorem. So it is classical periodic-truss mechanics applied to these frameworks: N0 or N1, not N2.
findings.reason: Symbol by symbol, the team's objects match classical periodic-truss mechanics. Team d0 (bars x dofs) is Lubensky's q=0 compatibility matrix C = Q^T. Team ae_rows are Lubensky's affine elongations e_aff = b_i eps_ij b_j (eq. 31). Team weights 1/2 = 1/|b|^2 are the spring constants k. Team S_cell = K_ee + B^T U* is Lubensky's (A4), k_ss - k_sr k_rr^-1 k_rs, and I checked this as exact equality. Team H^0 and H^1 are the zero modes N0 and states of self-stress NS, and H0 - H1 is the Maxwell-Calladine count. Team 'rank 1' is a single load-bearing self-stress, which is Norris's pentamode C = S x S (eqs. 43-45) with S the virial of that self-stress. The 'Master formula' is the virial sum_beta t_beta b_beta b_beta^T, with the motif terms collapsed by rigid-body equilibrium. Torque balance forces diag(tau)B to be symmetric, and the motif virial is 2 diag(tau) B. The team's own docstring credits the formula to 'Maxwell's Periodic Stress Theorem'. Several other claims are classical: the isotropy of D4 and E8 (4-designs), Cauchy relations C12 = C44 (central forces, no prestress), and the rational conic parametrizations. So the mechanism is N0. What is not in Norris (d = 2, 3, one node per cell) or Lubensky is the classification of these specific n-dimensional multi-node fold frameworks. Every twisted-cycle fold F_n(s), s in (0,1], is a rank-1 (n-dimensional pentamode) network. C4_nilp is pentamode with a traceless, zero-diagonal stress, so its bulk modulus is zero. The Hadamard E8 fold carries an indefinite sigma* = 2I + H8, with signature (4,4). The cyclic all-spinor E8 bases have rank 0. Under the team's definitions these are concrete local advances on untested cases: N1. N2 fails because frameworks and elasticity are not 'previously unlinked structures'; periodic trusses are the standard object of that theory. One more point: the closed-form trace (6n-2)/n is checked for n = 4..8 only and never proved, so it is a sampled claim.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: N1, exact: a theorem with a short proof that the team can now state for all n. Take the cross-polytope frameworks F(B) with bridge matrix B(s) = aI + tC, t > 0. The relaxed Cauchy-Born tensor has rank equal to the dimension of the span of {B^T diag(tau) B + 2 diag(tau) B : diag(tau) C symmetric}. Generically that equals the dimension of the space of diagonal symmetrizers of C, independent of s in (0,1]. Hence every uniquely symmetrizable C (twisted cycles C_n for all n >= 3, C4_nilp, H8) gives an n-dimensional pentamode network along the whole open fold. A non-symmetrizable C gives zero stiffness. Two decoupled symmetrizable blocks give rank 2 (my check). Instances: C4_nilp is a zero-bulk-modulus pentamode; Hadamard E8 has sigma* = 2I + H8 with signature (4,4). The mechanism (Lubensky 2015 eq. 33; Norris 2014 eqs. 43-45; the virial theorem) should be cited as known.

findings.first_pass_finding: The obstruction theorem (F_16 cannot fold to E_8 + E_8 or any orthogonal sum) is correct and elementary: it uses only that the roots of D_n lie in the endpoint lattice and that the root graph of D_n is connected.
findings.reason: Correct, and as elementary as the evaluator says. It needs only D_n contained in Gamma and the connectedness of the D_n root graph, and it holds for every R in O(n) and every nontrivial orthogonal sum, with no bars. The underlying fact, that an irreducible root system lies in one orthogonal summand (for example, D16 is not a root subsystem of E8 + E8), is classical root-system theory. I found no reading under which it adds a new invariant. Its value is as a clean recorded obstruction for the F_n program.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: Exact; N0 in mechanism, N1 at most as a recorded obstruction for this program. No periodic cross-polytope packing P_n + Lambda, with or without bars and under any rotation, equals a translate of a nontrivial orthogonal sum Gamma_1 (+) Gamma_2 of minimum 2. In particular F_16 cannot fold to E8 (+) E8; the block fold F_8 (+) F_8 -> E8 (+) E8 uses a different (product) motif, as the team itself notes.

areas.recovered_by_the_second_pass:
1. The Leech motif is a deep hole. My run gives four facts: no vector +-e_i lies in Gamma, every vector of 4Gamma has all coordinates of the same parity, the derived code has minimum weight 8, and there are no norm-24 odd vectors. Together they show that the points of Gamma_24 + e_0 nearest the origin are exactly the 48 points +-e_i at distance 1. Distance 1 is the Leech covering radius at this scale (sqrt 2 at minimum norm 4). So the team's motif P_24 is the vertex set of a deep hole of type A1^24, a cross-polytope Delone cell (Conway-Parker-Sloane). The team's realization then says: there is an index-48 sublattice (quotient (Z/2)^4 x Z/3) for which this deep-hole cross-polytope is a full coset transversal, with a basis 2e_i + c_i where each c_i is a minimal vector. This links the result to classical Leech hole theory. That is where the prior-art search should go, and it may help with the open global fold. I searched under several phrasings and found no statement of this coset-transversal property, but did not read SPLAG chapters 23-25 in full.
2. F4 helps the team on F1. The canonical seed Pi(I) fails on 28 contacts, all sampled ones same-axis +e_i/-e_i pairs. So the bar-constrained Leech arc does not follow from any generic recipe. That is evidence the bar content is non-trivial, not a defect.
3. A general theorem is within reach. On every case I checked, the team's AUDIT-019 data obey one statement, which I extended to a two-block case with rank 2: rank of S_cell = dimension of the diagonal symmetrizers of C, for all s in (0,1]. It has a short proof via torque balance and the virial theorem. The team can state it for all n instead of case by case. I also confirmed that Lubensky et al. 2015's eq. (A4) equals the team's Schur complement exactly. That gives a citable bridge from the team's 'sheaf' language to standard periodic-truss mechanics, at no loss.
4. The evaluator's independent work holds up. Its counts (196,560; 4,320; 28 negatives; both deltas) reproduce exactly with fully independent code. My route was different: an adjugate coset map, plus a minimal-vector enumeration derived from Gamma itself, without assuming a Golay code.
5. BW16 needs no code assumption. The minimal-vector enumeration is exhaustive over all integer vectors of norm 8, about 4 million candidates: 4,320 found and no shorter vectors.

findings.first_pass_finding: AUDIT-012's headline, that leave-one-catalog-out "decisively falsifies" the 185 km/s threshold of the gravity repo's wave7 study, is false as worded. The repo's own zero-parameter model with sigma* = 185.59 km/s fits every catalog including the held-out galaxies (chi-squared 1.57 for n = 6). Under wave7's own correlated fit the trained threshold in the galaxy hold-out is 145 km/s, not the 60.15 the audit reports. The fair statement is that the onset is not identified without the galaxy anchors and that the catalogs disagree.
findings.reason: The evaluator's facts reproduce. The 60.15 km/s in AUDIT-012 is an optimiser artifact: under wave7's correlated metric my profile puts the trained Hill threshold at 150 km/s (evaluator: 145; Delta chi2 <= 4 range 140 to 170). Probe 2's own diagonal metric gives 75 km/s (range 40 to 140). With nothing trained, the zero-parameter sigma* = 185.59 is acceptable on every catalog: galaxies chi2 1.34 (correlated) or 1.57 (diagonal) for n = 6, Milgrom optical 62.5 to 65.2 for 56, Milgrom rich 17.7 to 22.7 for 10, Angus 39.2 to 41.2 for 26, Kettula 17.7 to 19.2 for 28. A leave-one-catalog-out test cannot falsify a prediction that has no trained parameters, so 'decisively falsifies the 185 km/s threshold' is false as worded. The evaluator's replacement, 'not identified without the galaxy anchors', is too weak. The groups and clusters actively push against 185. Trained on the 120 non-galaxy systems, the Hill fit disfavours sc = 185 by Delta chi2 = 11.6 (correlated) or 14.4 (diagonal). Wave9's own one-parameter Jeans model puts sigma_J at 85 or 75 km/s and disfavours 185.59 by Delta chi2 = 14.0 or 17.1. Taken separately, Milgrom optical, Milgrom rich, Milgrom combined and X-ray plus lensing each prefer a lower onset (Delta chi2 at 185.59 from 3.7 to 12.2). The 6 galaxies alone need sigma_J >= 172.5. The trained model then fails the held-out galaxies (correlated metric: Hill 524 against 0.34 for MOND, Jeans 50 against 0.34), so the team's qualitative claim that the collapse is 'even sharper' under the native metric is right; only the number is wrong.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: In the wave7 and wave9 threshold families, the onset near 185 km/s is held in place by the 6 galaxy anchors, and the catalogs pull in opposite directions. The 120 group and cluster systems alone disfavour an onset at 185 km/s: Delta chi2 = 11.6 to 14.4 for the 3-parameter Hill fit, 14.0 to 17.1 for wave9's one-parameter Jeans model, best onset 75 to 150 km/s. The galaxies alone need sigma_J >= ~173 km/s. So the 'empirical group onset 180 to 190 km/s' leg of C-27's four-way convergence is a compromise between catalogs that disagree, not an independent measurement by groups. The zero-parameter sigma* = 185.59 is not falsified: its per-catalog chi2 is acceptable everywhere. The 60.15 km/s figure must be replaced by ~145 to 150 km/s (range 140 to 170). Label N1 (a newly found, concrete defect in a stated host claim, with a minimal reproducer), together with the SPARC to KiDS-1000 anchor result, which the evaluator also rated N1.

findings.first_pass_finding: The 0.00008 percent figure for the AeST slow-mode closure is measured against the team's own invariant initial condition, not the host repo's protocol. Under the protocol the same closure order gives 0.37 percent. The closure passes the host's 1 percent gate on the 5 slow preparations and fails on the fast-contaminated ones, and at backgrounds q_i = 0.03 and 0.1 the lowest order fails.
findings.reason: Every number reproduces. Under the protocol: H0 0.548% to 0.589%, H3 0.371% to 0.377%. H3 started on its own manifold: 0.000083% at k = 24, 0.0013% at k = 6. So the evaluator's facts stand. Two readings narrow the finding. (1) The 0.37% residual is not a closure error. It equals, to three digits, the difference between two exact four-state trajectories: the protocol's slow-subspace IC and the IC on the H3 graph (0.372% to 0.377%). The protocol IC sits 3.8% to 4.3% off the slow manifold in the fast coordinates. The team said exactly this in frontier_portals.md. The same holds at q_i = 0.03 (H3 1.11% to 1.14%, IC gap 1.12% to 1.14%) and q_i = 0.1 (H3 3.46% to 3.85%, IC gap 3.63% to 3.86%). Started on its own manifold, the closure tracks to 0.0007% to 0.18% even at q_i = 0.1. (2) No closure in (delta, theta) can pass the 60 fast-contaminated preparations. Phases 0 and pi give exact outputs base +- d with identical retained data, so any closure errs by at least max|d|: 1.33% (k = 6) to 5.06% (k = 24) already at eta = 0.001, and 13% to 506% at larger eta. Passing 5 of 65 is the most any two-variable closure can achieve, and the team's H3 sits close to that floor (1.70% against 1.33% at k = 6; 5.43% against 5.06% at k = 24). What remains of the finding: the headlines pair '0.55% / 0.00008%' without saying that the second figure uses the team's own IC, and q_i != 0.01 lies outside both the host protocol and the team's claim.
findings.strongest_surviving_claim: A zero-parameter quasi-static and Fenichel slow-manifold closure passes the host's 1% gate on all 5 protocol slow preparations at q_i = 0.01 (H0 0.55% to 0.59%, H3 0.37%), where the host's zero-pressure (24.6% to 27.4%) and adiabatic (up to 185%) closures fail. The remaining 0.37% is entirely the protocol IC's off-manifold component: from an IC on the closure's own graph, H3 tracks the exact solution to 1e-6 relative. The 60 contaminated preparations are unpassable by any closure that sees only retained data. Headline should read: 0.55% (H0) / 0.37% (H3) under the protocol; 0.00008% on the invariant manifold. Label N1 (a newly closed gate on an open host instance; the method, adiabatic elimination and Fenichel iteration, is standard).

findings.first_pass_finding: In the 16x16 Lindblad result the stated effective rate 2 gamma_tid + 2 g^2/(N^2 gamma_1) is the s = 0 Schur reduction. The true slow decay rate is 2 gamma_tid + 2 g^2/(gamma_CM - gamma_tid) + O(g^4), which differs at order g^2 when gamma_tid is not zero. The mathematics is standard adiabatic elimination (Azouit, Sarlette and Rouchon, arXiv 1603.04630), so it is known (the team labels it N2).
findings.reason: Mathematics confirmed. The block is [[-2gt, -2g], [2g, -2gcm]]. The slow rate is 2gt + 2g^2/(gcm-gt) + 2g^4/(gcm-gt)^3 + ..., which differs from Gamma_Schur = 2gt + 2g^2/gcm by 2g^2 gt/(gcm(gcm-gt)) at O(g^2) when gt != 0. S(lambda_slow) = lambda_slow exactly, and the product identity holds identically. But the team never calls Gamma_Schur the exact slow rate: it is presented as the s = 0 Schur complement, which is exact as stated, and the team's own Part B items 3 and 4 give the exact slow eigenvalue, the product identity, the O(N^-4) ratio (my numbers: 1.0654 at N = 5 to 1.00000036 at N = 100, gt = 0) and the Riccati lift that reaches the exact rate. So the correction is already inside the team's artifact. The narrow fault is that the headline lists present the IX/IY entry as the '1/N^2 Zeno sealing' rate without the 'leading order' qualifier. Prior art, symbol by symbol. ASR: d rho/dt = L0 + eps L1, with L0 fast. Lemma 1: a dissipative perturbation projects to L_s,1 with A_mu = S0^dag M_mu L1 S0. That is the team's -2gt on IX/IY (the Z(x)Z dephasing restricted to the slow algebra). Lemma 3: a Hamiltonian perturbation H1 yields a second-order Lindblad term with B_mu = 2 S0^dag M_mu L0 (L0^dag L0)^-1 H1 S0, the 4g^2/kappa-type rate. That is the team's 2g^2/gcm, with H1 = g X(x)Z and L0 = sqrt(gcm) Z(x)I. With gt counted as order eps, Gamma_Schur is the ASR expansion through eps^2, and the evaluator's correction is order eps^3. Exact difference: ASR assume the fast steady states are density operators supported on a subspace (a decoherence-free subspace). The team's kernel {rho : [rho, Z(x)I] = 0} is a two-block classical-quantum algebra, so ASR's lemmas do not apply verbatim. Also, the team keeps gt non-perturbative inside an exact Schur complement. Neither difference is new mathematics: the s = 0 Schur complement is the standard Markovian adiabatic-elimination reduction.

Not N2.

findings.first_pass_finding: The inertia box certifier is sound, and its method is known (verified LDL^T and interval methods for parametric matrices, for example Skalna, arXiv 1709.00853), so the method is known and the application to the truss is a local advance.
findings.reason: Sound in my test as well: 1,279 + 1,516 = 2,795 certified boxes, 10,232 + 12,128 = 22,360 exact sample points (corners, midpoints, seeded interior rationals), 0 violations. The certified classes include indefinite inertias (1,0,2), (2,0,1), (2,0,2), (3,0,1), (1,0,3) and (3,0,0), so soundness holds beyond positive definiteness. Prior art, mapped exactly. Skalna Theorem 3.1: A(p_c) positive definite plus regularity via rho(|A(p_c)^-1| B) < 1 (Beeck-type, Theorem 2.1) implies strongly positive definite; non-linear entries are handled by an affine-arithmetic transform to affine dependence; floating point. The team: exact rational LDL^T congruence C M(t_c) C^T = D at the midpoint, regularity via strict diagonal dominance of D + C(M(B) - M(t_c))C^T under rational interval arithmetic (natural interval extension instead of affine forms), plus branch-and-bound. Inertia constancy over the box then follows by continuity and Sylvester's law. The differences are these: exact rational instead of floating; any fixed inertia instead of PD only (an immediate generalisation of the same regularity-plus-continuity argument); a different but standard preconditioned regularity test; and subdivision. The team itself labels Probe 3 N1, so this finding agrees with the team. One overstatement the evaluator correctly noted: the full-box evaluator refuses by construction on straddling boxes, so 'isolates the singular line L1+L2 = 2' is supplied by the caller, not found by the method. The 373, 133 and 54 box counts are artifacts of that choice.
